findings.title: Local cache is populated before the device is persisted, allowing the device limit to be bypassed
findings.body: In tagDeviceUI the cache key is set with a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{}) before CreateOrUpdateDevice is called. When the device limit is reached, CreateOrUpdateDevice/updateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached and the request is rejected, but the key stays in the local cache for ~29 minutes. On the next request with the same X-Grafana-Device-Id, tagDeviceUI returns nil early (cache hit) and the anonymous user is authenticated without ever being recorded, effectively bypassing the new limit for the whole cache TTL. The cache entry should only be stored after a successful store call.

findings.title: Count-then-insert device limit check is not atomic
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice reads CountDevices and then performs the insert in a separate session. Under concurrent anonymous requests several goroutines can all observe count < deviceLimit and all insert, so the configured device_limit can be exceeded by an arbitrary amount. Enforcement needs to be done inside a transaction (or via a conditional insert) if the limit is meant to be a hard cap.

findings.title: rowsAffected == 0 is wrongly reported as ErrDeviceLimitReached for known devices on MySQL
findings.body: updateDevice maps rowsAffected == 0 to ErrDeviceLimitReached. On MySQL, an UPDATE that matches a row but changes no column values reports 0 affected rows (CLIENT_FOUND_ROWS not set), so an existing, within-expiry device whose client_ip/user_agent/updated_at are unchanged (same second precision) will be treated as over the limit and the user will be denied access. Use rows-matched semantics or an explicit existence check instead.

findings.title: Device tagging moved onto the synchronous auth path, adding DB round-trips per request
findings.body: TagDevice was previously executed in a background goroutine with its own timeout; it is now called inline in Authenticate. Every anonymous authentication that misses the local cache now blocks on a COUNT query plus an upsert against anon_device, and any DB slowness/latency now directly affects anonymous request latency and can fail authentication (errors other than ErrDeviceLimitReached are only logged, but the latency remains). Worth confirming this is intended and bounding it (context timeout).

findings.title: ErrDeviceLimitReached surfaces as a generic 500 to clients
findings.body: ErrDeviceLimitReached is created with fmt.Errorf and returned verbatim from Authenticate. The authn layer has no mapping for it, so a user blocked by the device limit gets an opaque internal error rather than a meaningful status/message (e.g. 429/403 with explanation). Define it with errutil so the API returns an actionable response.

findings.title: New auth.anonymous device_limit option is undocumented
findings.body: cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit is read from [auth.anonymous] device_limit but the option is not added to conf/defaults.ini, conf/sample.ini, or the configuration docs. Operators have no discoverable way to learn about the setting or its default (0 = unlimited).

findings.title: anonymousDeviceLimit initialized to undefined infers type `undefined`
findings.body: `anonymousDeviceLimit = undefined` without an explicit annotation gives the property the type `undefined`, while the backend always sends a number (0 when unset) via merge(). Consumers that read it as a number will fail type checking, and the declared `number | undefined` in GrafanaConfig never actually becomes undefined. Annotate as `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined = undefined`.
